rules.action: Radial access preferred over femoral for all PCI.
rules.rationale: Radial access reduces access-site bleeding, vascular complications, and all-cause mortality.
rules.detail: Femoral access reserved for cases requiring large-bore sheath (MCS device), complex anatomy precluding radial, or operator preference with anatomical indication.

rules.action: Use large-lumen guide (≥7Fr); 8Fr preferred when DK-Crush is planned.
rules.rationale: Bilateral kissing balloon inflation requires simultaneous large-bore access. Guide damping causes ostial occlusion.
rules.detail: Confirm non-dampened pressure waveform before wiring. Partially disengage guide if waveform is dampened.

rules.action: Confirm cardiac surgical backup availability before proceeding with unprotected LM PCI.
rules.rationale: Complex anatomy, reduced EF, or technical failure may require emergent CABG.
rules.detail: Pre-procedural Heart Team discussion recommended for elective cases. Size arterial access for potential MCS device insertion.

rules.action: Consider guide extension catheter (GEC) to improve device deliverability.
rules.rationale: GEC provides distal support without the ostial trauma risk of a stiffer guide.
rules.detail: Deploy GEC only after confirming co-axial alignment. Prefer GEC over escalating guide stiffness.

rules.action: Judkins Right as first choice; escalate to Amplatz only if support is inadequate.
rules.rationale: Amplatz guides carry higher risk of ostial trauma in tortuous/angulated RCA. Deep-seating or GEC are preferable escalation steps.
rules.caution: Avoid aggressive Amplatz engagement — ostial injury risk is significant in tortuous RCA.

rules.action: Prioritise coaxial alignment over backup force. Select guide shape by graft origin and approach.
rules.rationale: Aggressive backup support risks ostial graft injury. Coaxial engagement is the primary goal.
rules.detail: Transfemoral: JR4 or Hockey Stick (right-sided grafts); AL1 or left coronary bypass (left-sided grafts). Right transradial: AL1 for left-sided grafts; right-sided engagement challenging. Left transradial: AL or MP. GEC useful when ostial engagement is inadequate. Use shorter guides for very distal or sequential graft lesions.

rules.action: Strongly prefer PCI of the native coronary over the graft if technically feasible.
rules.rationale: Native vessel PCI avoids the embolic and no-reflow risks inherent to degenerated graft intervention.
rules.detail: Applicable particularly when the SVG is degenerated. Discuss feasibility of native vessel approach at case planning.

rules.action: Establish MCS before wiring if at all possible. Plan access site for large-bore device insertion.
rules.rationale: MCS support before coronary instrumentation reduces risk of haemodynamic collapse at the critical step.
rules.detail: Femoral access may be required for MCS device. Minimise contrast volume. Treat culprit only if multivessel disease present.
rules.caution: Do not delay treatment of the culprit to place MCS if the patient is actively deteriorating — MCS and culprit PCI can proceed in parallel in extremis.
